doc.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995

title: Helen Humes, the Basie rhythm section and piano-led bands
summary: He praises the tight Basie rhythm section and says a pianist leader keeps a rhythm section together.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Helen Humes. She was with Basie for a while wasn’t she?
Yeah. She was with Basie. Now she could have told you some things about Basie and the band. You would have loved to talk to her. Too bad she’s gone.
Was the Basie band something that you listened to off and on? We’ve talked with some people about the sound of their rhythm section. Was that something that —
Oh, they had a tight rhythm section, yeah. They were together. You don’t find that anymore. Yeah with Papa Jo Jones and whoever the bass player was, and Basie, and Freddie on guitar. Jesus.
Can’t do any better than that.

Couldn’t beat that. Yeah they had a thing going. But bands are not like that today. They’re not, well to have a band like that, the piano player’s got to be the leader, to keep a rhythm section together. And most days now, it’s a trumpet player or a saxophone player, and they don’t stress that as much.
